summary.intent: Run load tests against the cipher-box staging API at increasing client counts (10, 20, 30, then 50, 75, 100, 200) to establish performance baselines and identify the scaling ceiling for a single instance. Additionally, diagnose which part of the uploadFile flow is the primary latency bottleneck.
summary.outcome: Full scaling baselines documented from 10–200 clients; 100 clients is the practical ceiling (zero errors, ~24 ops/s), with first errors appearing at 200 clients (4 errors). Prometheus analysis confirmed Kubo IPFS pinning accounts for ~95% of uploadFile latency (3 pins per upload at ~1.73s mean each). Results committed to `.planning/baselines/19-someguy-ipns-baselines.md`.

repo: The load-test GitHub Actions workflow uses the `staging` GitHub environment for secret scoping — this causes the UI to show 'Deploying to staging' even though no deployment occurs; it is cosmetic only.

The `uploadFile` SDK operation makes 5 sequential API calls: 3× POST /ipfs/upload (ciphertext, file metadata, folder metadata) + POST /ipns/publish-batch (file IPNS) + POST /ipns/publish (folder IPNS).
Staging secrets (STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET, STAGING_API_URL) are scoped to the `staging` GitHub environment, not repository-level secrets.
release-please is triggered by conventional commit prefixes — `chore(ci):` commits do not kick off a release.

The `staging` branch protection on `main` had a stale required check `Verify E2E Passed` from a previous workflow; the new consolidated CI job is named `SDK E2E Tests` and needed to be added as required separately.
Throughput scales sub-linearly above 30 clients: 10x clients yields only ~5.4x throughput at 100 clients, plateauing around 24 ops/s.

code.finding: The `test:single` script used `--testPathPattern` which is a Jest CLI flag, not valid in Vitest. Fixed by removing it; Vitest accepts file filter patterns as positional args.

Using `pnpm test:single -- <scenario>` does not correctly pass the scenario as a Vitest file filter — args after `--` go into CAC's separate bucket. Fixed by calling `pnpm exec vitest run --no-coverage <scenario>` directly.
The job lacked `environment: staging`, causing all staging env vars to be empty. Adding it fixed secret access but introduces the cosmetic 'Deploying to staging' label in the GitHub UI.
Added `concurrency` group `load-test-<environment>` so parallel trigger calls queue instead of running simultaneously against the same staging API, preventing result interference.

Default `timeout-minutes: 30` caused cancellation when running all 5 scenarios at high client counts. Increased to 60 minutes. The scenario filter fix reduced per-run time to ~5 minutes for mixed-workload alone.
Baseline doc updated with full 10/20/30/50/75/100/200-client scaling tables, per-operation latency breakdown, Prometheus upload flow analysis, and bottleneck identification.

workflow: Running multiple `gh run watch` instances simultaneously (6 at 3s poll intervals = ~120 req/min) quickly exhausts the GitHub API rate limit (5000 req/hour). Use a single status check instead of concurrent watchers.
Prometheus histogram buckets allow computing approximate percentiles via linear interpolation between bucket boundaries; mean can be computed exactly as sum/count.
When cherry-picking commits to rename them for a different conventional commit type, close the original PR first and open a new one from the renamed branch.

friction: Initial load test runs all failed because `--testPathPattern` (Jest) was used instead of Vitest's positional arg pattern — required a bug fix PR before any results could be collected.
Missing `environment: staging` on the workflow job caused all staging secrets/vars to be empty, requiring a second fix in the same PR.

The scenario filter bug (`--` separator not working with the npm script) caused all 5 scenarios to run instead of just `mixed-workload`, making 10/20/30-client runs take 16+ minutes and causing 50/75/100-client runs to exceed the 30-minute timeout and get cancelled.
Running 6 concurrent `gh run watch` processes (3 original + 3 re-watches) at 3-second intervals burned through the GitHub API rate limit, blocking status checks for ~1 hour.
Rate limit persisted longer than expected — two separate 60-second and 5-minute wait attempts both still hit the limit.
The `gh run watch` command exited prematurely on some runs due to the deployment environment approval step, requiring re-watches that then hit rate limits.
open_items: Fix the scenario filtering for the 10/20/30 baseline runs — they ran all 5 scenarios instead of just mixed-workload, so those results include noise from other scenarios.

Investigate and potentially fix the 0.26% async DHT propagation error rate seen in Prometheus (324 errors across all runs) — these are fire-and-forget and don't affect clients but may indicate DHT health issues.
Explore Kubo pinning optimizations to reduce the ~1.73s mean pin latency that dominates uploadFile: faster storage backend, concurrent pins, or pin batching.

Consider moving STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET, STAGING_THROTTLE_BYPASS_SECRET, and STAGING_API_URL to repository-level secrets to remove the `environment: staging` field and eliminate the misleading 'Deploying to staging' UI label.
Determine whether the 4 errors at 200 clients are upload timeouts, connection resets, or 5xx responses — error type was identified as present but not fully classified.
Run 150-client test to narrow down the exact threshold between 100 (zero errors) and 200 (first errors) for a more precise single-instance capacity number.
